review_output.summary: [High] Returning at '\0' without advancing *i hangs index-bounded loops when the bound overshoots the terminator
review_output.failure_scenario: Impact: lv_text_get_width(_with_flags) (while(i < length), :399/:432) and lv_text_utf8_get_char_id (while(i < byte_id), :772) relied on the decoder stepping past '\0'; now i sticks at the terminator and the loop never exits. In-tree trigger: text ending in a truncated UTF-8 sequence such as "A\xC3" — lv_text_utf8_get_byte_id over-counts (byte_id 3), lv_label_get_letter_pos calls lv_text_get_width_with_flags(txt, 3) which hangs at i=2 (with BIDI, lv_text_encoded_get_char_id hangs). Public API callers with length > strlen now hang instead of over-reading. Remedy: add `&& txt[i] != '\0'` to these loops and/or clamp lv_text_utf8_get_byte_id at the terminator; add a regression test e.g. lv_text_get_width("A\xC3", 3, ...) terminating.

review_output.summary: [Medium] lv_label_get_letter_on infinite loop when a recolor label's last line ends inside a `#` command
review_output.failure_scenario: Impact: last-line bound is strlen+1 (lv_label.c:451); with text like "ab#" the decoder now stays at '\0', lv_text_is_cmd(&cmd_state, '\0') returns true in PAR state (lv_text.c:160-165), and the `continue` at lv_label.c:487-495 loops forever — pressing past the last glyph in a textarea/roller hangs the UI thread or causes a watchdog reset. Remedy: break when bidi_txt[i] == '\0' or i did not advance; pass `letter` rather than bidi_txt[i] to lv_text_is_cmd; add a regression test.

review_output.summary: [Medium] NULL/terminator guard only in the UTF-8 backend; lv_text_encoded_next contract now depends on LV_TXT_ENC
review_output.failure_scenario: Impact: lv_text_iso8859_1_next (:847-853) still dereferences NULL and advances past '\0', so in ASCII builds the OOB fix does not apply and the new NULL test crashes / empty-string test fails. Remedy: apply the same guard in lv_text_iso8859_1_next or do the NULL check once at the shared entry, and document it in lv_text_private.h:219-227.

review_output.summary: [Medium] Decoder contract changed (no advance at terminator, NULL accepted) but doc comments not updated
review_output.failure_scenario: Impact: docs at lv_text.c:628-635 and lv_text_private.h:219-226 still say txt must be a terminated string and *i always moves to the next char; now NULL is accepted and *i stays at '\0', so loops assuming progress (lv_text.c:772) can't learn this from the docs. Remedy: update both doc blocks to state NULL returns 0 and *i does not move at NULL/'\0'.

review_output.summary: [Medium] Truncated multibyte sequences and invalid lead bytes are untested
review_output.failure_scenario: Impact: "\xC3", "\xE2\x82", "\xF0\x9F\x98" (the realistic old OOB trigger) and the invalid-lead else{(*i)++;} branch (:699-701) have no tests, so a regression reintroducing the over-read would go unnoticed. Remedy: add tests decoding these with repeated calls asserting ofs never exceeds strlen; add a "\x80A" case.

review_output.summary: [Medium] No test covers length-bounded callers whose bound runs past the terminator
review_output.failure_scenario: Impact: the change turns an over-read in lv_text_get_width(_with_flags) and lv_text_utf8_get_char_id into an infinite loop (e.g. lv_text_get_width("A", 5, ...)), and no test calls them with length/byte_id > strlen. Remedy: add tests with an over-long bound asserting termination with the strlen result (forcing a txt[i] != '\0' guard).

review_output.summary: [Low] New tests assume UTF-8 encoding with no encoding guard
review_output.failure_scenario: Impact: under LV_TXT_ENC ISO8859-1/ASCII builds the NULL test dereferences NULL and the "é" tests fail. Remedy: wrap them in #if LV_TXT_ENC == LV_TXT_ENC_UTF8, or make both decoder backends behave the same.

review_output.summary: [Low] "ofs unchanged" assertion cannot distinguish unchanged from reset to 0
review_output.failure_scenario: Impact: ofs starts at 0 and the test asserts 0 (also at :162), so a regression that resets ofs would pass and the comment over-claims. Remedy: start ofs at a non-zero value (e.g. 3) and assert it is preserved.

review_output.summary: [Low] 3 of the 5 new tests pass on the merge base and don't test the fix
review_output.failure_scenario: Impact: "A", "é", "éA" behave identically before and after the change and only exercise the lv_text_encoded_letter_next_2 wrapper, yet read as coverage of the fix. Remedy: extend them with end-of-string calls or add direct lv_text_encoded_next tests, or label them as baseline decode tests.

review_output.summary: [Low] Guard comment covers only half the check and differs from the file's style
review_output.failure_scenario: Impact: the comment says "not null" but the '\0' half is the actual OOB fix and is unmentioned, risking later removal; the file uses tight /*...*/ comments and explicit `return 0;` for early returns. Remedy: e.g. `/*NULL or end of string: don't step past the terminator*/` and `return 0;`.

review_output.summary: [Low] Raw "é" literals where the file uses hex-escaped UTF-8 bytes
review_output.failure_scenario: Impact: expected bytes depend on source-file encoding and compiler execution charset, so the 0xE9 / ofs==2 expectations may break on other toolchains. Remedy: use "\xc3\xa9" and "\xc3\xa9" "A" like the neighbouring tests.

review_output.summary: [Nitpick] New test names break the file's test_txt_ prefix convention
review_output.failure_scenario: Impact: these 5 tests are the only test_lv_* names in the suite, hurting grep and naming consistency. Remedy: rename to test_txt_encoded_letter_next_2_should_...

result_text:
The review's verdict is **BLOCK**. The fix stops one out-of-bounds read, but it can now make text measurement and label hit-testing loop forever. I sent all 12 findings in the report above to the findings tool (1 High, 5 Medium, 5 Low, 1 Nitpick). I left out the one finding that verification refuted. Six specialist reviewers covered both changed files, and independent verifiers confirmed 6 of the 7 Medium-and-above findings.

**What blocks it.** The new check stops the UTF-8 decoder from moving past the end-of-string byte. Some callers loop until a byte count is reached rather than until the end of the string, and they now never finish:
- **Width and index loops** (`lv_text.c:399`, `:432`, `:772`) hang when the count runs past the end of the string. Text ending in a cut-off multibyte character, like `"A\xC3"`, causes exactly that through `lv_label_get_letter_pos`. Before this change these loops read a byte or two too far and then stopped.
- **`lv_label_get_letter_on`** hangs on a label with recolor on whose last line ends inside a `#` color command (e.g. `"ab#"`). Pressing past the last character in a textarea or roller freezes the UI thread.

**Medium findings to fix as well:**
- The new check exists only in the UTF-8 decoder. The ISO-8859-1 decoder still reads through NULL and past the end, so behaviour depends on the build's encoding setting.
- The doc comments still describe the old behaviour.
- There are no tests for cut-off multibyte sequences or for lengths that run past the end of the string.

**Fix:** stop those loops at the end-of-string byte (add `txt[i] != '\0'` to their conditions) and add regression tests for both hangs.

No spec was found beyond the commit message, so nothing was checked against requirements.
